faq.q: What is the main difference between the Astondoa 40 and Princess V58?
faq.a: The Astondoa 40 is 12.5m long and takes up to 9 passengers, while the Princess V58 is 17.7m and holds 12. The Princess V58 is larger, with a flybridge and more deck space, making it better for bigger groups and longer trips. The Astondoa 40 is more compact and sporty, ideal for a quick coastal outing.

faq.q: Which yacht is better for a large group or party?
faq.a: The Princess V58 is better for larger groups, with capacity for 12 passengers and a flybridge that offers extra sunbathing and social space. The Astondoa 40 is limited to 9 passengers and has a more streamlined layout, so it’s best for smaller, more intimate gatherings.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks on either yacht?

data.body_html:
Choosing between the Astondoa 40 vs Princess V58 for your Marbella charter comes down to group size, budget, and how you want to spend your day on the water. The Astondoa 40 is a sporty 12.5m motor yacht that fits up to 9 guests and starts at €749 for a 2-hour cruise from Puerto Banús. The Princess V58 is a larger 17.7m flybridge yacht that accommodates 12 passengers, with pricing available on request. Both include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT. This comparison covers specs, pricing, and practical tips to help you decide which yacht suits your Marbella charter.

Astondoa 40 vs Princess V58: Key Specs at a Glance

Here’s a quick side-by-side of the two yachts to help you compare:

Capacity and Space: Who Fits Where?

The Astondoa 40 is certified for up to 9 passengers, making it ideal for small families, couples, or a group of friends. Its layout is open and social, with a forward sunpad and a comfortable cockpit. The Princess V58, with 12-person capacity, offers significantly more deck space, including a flybridge with second helm station, additional sun loungers, and a larger saloon. If you’re planning a party or need room to spread out, the Princess V58 wins. For an intimate coastal cruise, the Astondoa 40 feels perfectly proportioned.

Pricing and Value: Astondoa 40 vs Princess V58

The Astondoa 40 offers transparent, fixed pricing: €749/2h, €1,099/4h, €1,599/6h, and €2,299/8h. All rates include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% Spanish VAT. The Princess V58 is priced on request — typically higher due to its size and luxury. If you’re on a budget or want a quick half-day trip, the Astondoa 40 provides excellent value. For a full-day luxury experience with a larger group, the Princess V58 is worth the premium. Contact us via WhatsApp for a Princess V58 quote.

Performance and Handling

The Astondoa 40 is powered by twin engines that deliver a sporty ride, perfect for zipping along the coast from Puerto Banús to Cabopino or Cala del Faro. Its smaller size makes it easy to anchor in secluded coves. The Princess V58, with more powerful engines, offers a smoother ride at higher speeds and greater range for longer itineraries, such as a day trip to Estepona or Sotogrande. Both yachts are handled by our licensed skippers, so you can relax and enjoy the scenery.

Which Yacht Is Best for Your Marbella Charter?

Choose the Astondoa 40 if you have a group of 9 or fewer, want a budget-friendly option, and prefer a sporty, compact yacht for a half-day outing. Choose the Princess V58 if you need space for up to 12 guests, want a flybridge for sunbathing, and are planning a full-day charter where luxury and comfort are priorities. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include all essentials, so your decision hinges on group size and budget.
